change.describe: branch `pr-67876-flat` of sentry-67876-flat against f3b740199ef0b8057c2c68a377fd3b4d42346deb (merge-base f3b7401)
change.title: pr-67876-flat
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: KeyError (500) when the existing Integration has no `sender` metadata
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes `sender` is always set. It is only set when `build_integration` receives `state["sender"]` (line 376). That happens in the webhook path (`webhook.py:204`). The UI pipeline state never carries a sender, and `test_integration.py:303-310` asserts exactly that: an Integration created through the setup flow has no `sender` key. An Integration with no OrganizationIntegration is the normal state after a Sentry org removes the integration while the GitHub App stays installed. Re-installing it from another org then reaches this line and raises KeyError, so the user gets a 500 instead of the error dialog. Use `.get` chains. Decide explicitly what a missing sender means (reject with `error(...)`, or fall back), and add a test for it.

findings.title: No ownership check when the Integration row doesn't exist yet
findings.body: If `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises DoesNotExist, the view calls `next_step()` without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to anything. The authenticated GitHub user is only checked against `sender` when the Integration row already exists (lines 493-505). Whoever completes OAuth as any GitHub user can supply an arbitrary `installation_id` in the query string (line 448 prefers `request.GET` over saved state). They can then bind that installation to their org until the `installation` webhook has created the row. The PR's goal is to verify the installer, so this window should either be closed (for example by checking the installation's account or sender via the GitHub API in `build_integration`) or called out as a known gap.

findings.title: Network failures in the token exchange and user lookup are unhandled
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` (line 423) sits outside the `try`, so a connection error or SSL error raises and returns a 500. The sibling `OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token` catches `SSLError` and `ConnectionError` (`src/sentry/identity/oauth2.py:287-302`). `get_user_info` (line 434) calls `raise_for_status()` (`src/sentry/identity/github/provider.py:16`). Any non-2xx response from api.github.com, such as a revoked token or a rate limit, raises HTTPError and gives a 500 rather than `error(...)`. Wrap both calls and return the existing error dialog, which the popup flow needs in order to post a failure message back.

findings.title: Authorize URL is built by string interpolation without encoding
findings.body: `redirect_uri` and `state` are interpolated raw into the query string. `redirect_uri` is a full URL, so it should go through `urlencode`. The test pins the raw form (`redirect_uri=http://testserver/extensions/github/setup/`). Using `urlencode` would produce a correct URL and keep working if the host or path ever contains reserved characters.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` no longer tests the 404 path
findings.body: The callback is sent with `state=ddd023d8...`, which differs from the pipeline signature `9cae5e88...` used everywhere else. The request therefore fails at the state check (`integration.py:412`), and the test asserts the generic "Invalid installation request." message. The `ApiError` 404 to `IntegrationError("The GitHub installation could not be found.")` path in `build_integration` (lines 354-356) now has no coverage, although the test name and the 404 stub still claim to cover it. Use the valid state so the flow reaches `build_integration` and assert the original message. If the state-mismatch case is also wanted, add it as a separate test.

findings.title: Positive and edge cases of the new sender check are untested
findings.body: Only the mismatch case (`test_github_user_mismatch`) exercises lines 493-505. Cases with no coverage: an existing active Integration whose sender matches the OAuth user (should proceed), an Integration with no `sender` (see the KeyError finding), a non-active Integration, and the `OAuthLoginView` branches for a failed token exchange or a missing `login`. In `test_github_installed_on_another_org` the Integration is deleted before the retry, so it takes the DoesNotExist branch rather than the match branch.

contracts.action: New OAuth login step (`OAuthLoginView`) is inserted before `GitHubInstallation` in the GitHub integration pipeline
contracts.before_after: Before, the first request with `installation_id` went straight to the install checks. Now the first request redirects to GitHub authorize with `state=pipeline.signature`. The callback verifies `state`, exchanges the code, fetches `/user`, and stores `github_authenticated_user` in pipeline state before `next_step()`. The sibling `OAuth2CallbackView` also catches SSLError and ConnectionError around the exchange, and this one does not.
contracts.visible_effect: Installers are bounced through the GitHub authorize screen. Errors render `github-integration-failed.html` and post a failure message to the opener.
contracts.failure_mode: State mismatch, a missing `access_token` or a missing `login` render the error dialog. A network exception in `safe_urlopen`, or an HTTPError in `get_user_info`, is unhandled and returns a 500, which the user sees as a blank or error page in the popup.

contracts.action: Compare the authenticated GitHub user to `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` before binding an existing Integration to a new org
contracts.equivalent_path: The webhook creation path that stores `sender`: `src/sentry/integrations/github/webhook.py:201-209`
contracts.before_after: The check was not there before. `sender` is only stored by the webhook-created Integration. Integrations created via the UI pipeline have no `sender` (see `test_integration.py:303-310`).
contracts.visible_effect: A mismatch shows the generic "Invalid installation request." dialog.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing `sender` key raises KeyError and returns a 500. Cases with no Integration row skip the check.

contracts.before_after: Behaviour is the same. A repository-wide grep finds no other users of `FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR`.

summary: The change adds a GitHub OAuth step and a sender-vs-authenticated-user check to the install pipeline. I found two real bugs and one test problem. `integration.metadata[\"sender\"][\"login\"]` raises KeyError for Integrations created through the UI flow, which have no `sender`. Network and HTTP errors in the token exchange and `/user` lookup return a 500. `test_installation_not_found` now fails on state mismatch and no longer covers the 404 path. There is also a possible ownership gap when no Integration row exists yet, and the positive paths of the sender check are untested. The `pipeline_advancer.py` change is a harmless inline.
